study: VQ4DiT paper-protocol reproduction, not additive VQDM
precision: FP32, TF32 disabled, no activation quantization
loss: sum of mean squared errors of all 28 block outputs plus sum of per-layer equation9 penalties
deployment: one hard index per vector, FP32 codebooks and unquantized parameters; training ratios excluded
unspecified_details: The paper does not state whether batch16 includes CFG duplication. Here it means16 images with32 conditional/unconditional forward records; accumulation preserves this batch.
RMSprop alpha0.9 and100 Lloyd iterations are taken from the author release; the paper only specifies optimizer and learning rates.
Block biases are trainable at1e-4 as in the author parameter groups; non-block parameters are frozen.
The paper does not specify the reduction across layers in equation9. Penalties are normalized by vector count per layer and then summed, like the displayed block reconstruction sum.
The paper does not publish seeds or exact VAE variant. The author script default ema VAE is pinned by revision and file hashes; the FP control is measured again.
Sequential teacher DDPM50 states provide500 optimizer updates over10 batches. This follows the stated500 iterations, not the release's50000 updates. The queued reproduction evaluates DDPM50 only.
release_differences: Missing download, global_var and kmeans_sr imports and inconsistent CLI/compress_model API are bypassed by a separate runner; upstream files remain unchanged.
Codebooks are trainable jointly with ratios from the beginning, as described by equations10/11, unlike the release's initially frozen books.
Ratios start equal as stated in section4.1, not inverse-distance-biased as in prepare_sim.
The equation9 absolute-value polarization is used, not the release's conditional quadratic surrogate.
Hard assignment is selected by argmax after calibration, whether or not the early-hardening threshold was reached. Evaluation never uses a soft mixture.
Calibration uses eval mode to avoid independent class-dropout in student and teacher; gradients to codebooks, ratios and block biases remain enabled.
